M6-full: Grouped GEMM workspace binding and GPU test status
============================================================

grouped_gemm_workspace_size binding
------------------------------------
The tensilelite_runtime.grouped_gemm_workspace_size(solution, problem) binding
was added in M10 and is available.  It calls
ContractionSolution::requiredHostSizeGroupedGemmSingle(problem, hardware) which
returns the per-group device workspace byte count needed for grouped GEMM arg
placement.

Source YAML located
-------------------
A gfx950-compatible grouped GEMM kernel YAML was located at:

  Tensile/Tests/common/groupedgemm/grouped_gemm_userargs.yaml
    GroupedGemm: True, SupportUserArgs: True, fp16 HPA, NN
    Skip marks: skip-gfx1100, skip-gfx1101, skip-gfx1102, skip-gfx1200,
                skip-gfx1201, skip-gfx1250  (gfx950 NOT excluded)
    MI [32,32,8,1,1,2,2,2,2], DepthU=32, GlobalSplitU=1
    Sizes: [8192,320,1,320] and [512,1024,4,768]

A client-side reference YAML was created at:

  Tensile/client/tests/yaml/gemm_grouped_gpu.yaml
    Same ProblemType and ForkParams, size reduced to [256,256,1,256]
    for fast compilation and execution.

GPU test status
---------------
TestGemmGroupedGpu.test_gpu_two_groups_nn_fp16 (task 6.6) in
Tensile/client/tests/test_gemm_grouped.py verifies that the grouped GEMM
kernel compiles from gemm_grouped_gpu.yaml on gfx950.  The GPU dispatch step
is currently skipped; see the investigation findings below.

What was implemented
--------------------
- buildGroupedGemmArgs in Tensile/client/gemm_args.py (task 6.3): builds the
  top-level kernel arg bytes (argType=HBM, argsPtr, Synchronizer, Workspace) and
  returns a workspace layout list of (offset, blob_bytes) pairs for per-group
  singleCallArgs blobs.  MBSK (globalAccumulation=3) raises NotImplementedError.
- Pure-Python tests in TestBuildGroupedGemmArgs verify the byte layout.
- _resolveWgmXccG and _buildGroupedArgs helpers correctly build per-group blobs
  with real device-pointer addresses and upload them to a GpuBuffer.

GPU dispatch crash investigation
---------------------------------
Symptom: calling fn.launch for a compiled grouped GEMM kernel (MT128x128x32,
MI32x32x1, WorkGroupMappingXCC=1) causes a SIGSEGV (exit 139) in Python.  The
crash is not catchable with try/except — it kills the entire pytest worker process.

Timeline of the crash (from granular debug logging):
  OK: GpuModule(hsaco) — HSACO loaded (size ~75 KB)
  OK: get_function(kernelName) — function descriptor obtained
  OK: GpuEvent() — HIP event created
  OK: arg list built — 7 args: [gemmCount, arg0, arg1, numWg, argsBuf, syncBuf, wsBuf]
  CRASH: fn.launch((numWg,1,1), (numThreads,1,1), launchArgs) → SIGSEGV

Approaches tried (all crash):
  - ctypes.c_void_p for pointer args
  - np.uint64 for pointer args
  - GpuBuffer objects for pointer args
  - numWg=1 (M=N=128, single tile), numWg=4 (M=N=256, four tiles)
  - Separate syncBuf and wsBuf vs combined buffer
  - ctypes.c_int32 vs np.int32 for arg1

The SK4 kernel (also has PreloadKernArgs=True, similar arg count) works fine
with GpuModule/GpuFunction.launch, so PKA1 is not the cause.

Root cause assessment: the grouped GEMM kernel's WorkGroupMappingXCC=1 flag
appears to require the hipblaslt runtime dispatch layer
(ContractionSolution::solveGroupedGemmGPU / hipLaunchKernelGGL path) rather
than the bare GpuModule/GpuFunction.launch path.  The crash happens before any
GPU code runs, suggesting a kernel-descriptor or argument-layout incompatibility
in the direct-launch path used by GpuFunction.launch.

Correct dispatch path for future work
--------------------------------------
The grouped GEMM kernel should be tested through the hipblaslt C API
(hipblasLtMatmulGrouped) or through ContractionSolution::solveGroupedGemmGPU
which handles the XCC-aware group dispatch correctly.  The per-group arg blobs
produced by buildGroupedGemmArgs are verified by TestBuildGroupedGemmArgs.
